parts.title: The Rockslide
parts.text: Halfway up the mountain trail, a loud crack echoed across the cliffs, and a wave of loose rock and mud swept over the path ahead. Dalia's classmates began to scream, and **hysteria** spread through the group faster than the dust. Their guide, Mr. Quill, lay on the ground clutching his ankle. Everett glanced at the dark clouds and realized the situation was **urgent**. Another slide looked **imminent**.

parts.title: Taking Charge
parts.text: Dalia took one slow breath and kept her **composure**. "Everyone sit down and listen," she said firmly. At summer camp she had learned first aid, and she knew what was **crucial**: keep the guide still and warm. Soren scrambled up a boulder where his phone found one weak bar of signal and used it to **summon** a rescue team. Everett's job was to count heads and keep everyone talking quietly.

parts.title: Help from Above
parts.text: The operator promised to **expedite** a helicopter because the weather was turning. Within forty minutes a **paramedic** swung down on a cable and moved to **stabilize** Mr. Quill's ankle with a splint. Every student had been in **jeopardy**, she said, yet the only **casualty** was the guide's broken bone. She also warned that the emotional **trauma** of a frightening event can leave people shaky for days, so no one should feel embarrassed to talk about it.

parts.title: Back on Solid Ground
parts.text: That night, Dalia's hands finally began to shake. Her teacher told her that being brave never means feeling no fear. It means doing the next right thing anyway. Soren and Everett nodded. Each of them had done something small, and together those small jobs had kept a frightening afternoon from becoming a tragedy. Dalia decided to take another first-aid course the very next summer.

secretPassage.instructions: Read the passage below. Fill in each blank with the correct vocabulary word from the word bank.
secretPassage.passage:
Soren's grandmother volunteered at a river rescue station, and she loved telling the story of her busiest night. The call that came in was _(1)_: two kayakers were stuck on a rock as the water rose. She had to _(2)_ every volunteer in town with a single phone message, because the flood was _(3)_. Standing on the bank, she kept her _(4)_ even though the frightened onlookers were close to _(5)_. "The most _(6)_ thing," she says, "is to speak slowly and give each person one job."

A _(7)_ waited in the boat, ready to _(8)_ anyone who was hurt. The mayor promised to _(9)_ the arrival of a second boat. Both kayakers had been in serious _(10)_, yet they stepped ashore shivering and smiling, wrapped in blankets. Their only lasting _(11)_ was a fear of deep water. Thanks to the quick work of the whole town, the night ended without a single _(12)_.
